doc.title: Jim Hall — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Musically, he has enabled you to do some very interesting projects with ArtistShare.
Yeah.
So that first one is the one you were talking about. That was Magic Meeting.
Yeah.
It was the Vanguard Trio.
Oh, right, yeah.
The next thing you did was in collaboration—another duo collaboration that was, again, a pushing of the envelope. That was with Geoff Keezer. Free Association with Geoff Keezer.
Yeah. We… I’d have to, I’d have to hear that again. Where did we do that?
That done in the studio. I think it’s a blue cover. And it’s just you and Geoff. It’s a duo recording. That was now, mm, six years ago.
Do you remember any of the tunes or anything?
I don’t, but if we take a break, maybe I should pull those couple of CDs. What do you think, Ken?
Okay, later on. Here’s a question. What does Geoff play on these things?
What does Geoff Keezer play?
Yeah.
Piano. You’re not placing Geoff at the moment, right?
I’m not and I can’t remember anything about…
Very young piano player. He was once managed by Mary Ann Topper when he first started out.

Oh, oh. Jesus, yeah. I remember that. Yeah, and we both were… Yeah, Geoff is amazing. And then we worked together in the quartet and everything, yeah. Yeah, that’s great. Yeah, I don’t remember what we played, but he’s, he’s incredible. Can go in any direction, you know, and…
Mm-hmm. I think he plays inside the…
Yeah, yeah. He, they live out in, near San Francisco now.
Oh.
Yeah. That’s so stupid that I forgot, forgot his name. (laughs) Well, when I work with so many people, you know…
